title: Bulk OPE Coefficients of the $E$-Series Virasoro Minimal Models
authors: Amaury Lhoste, Jiaxin Qiao, Masahito Yamazaki
abstract: We present bulk-primary operator-product coefficients for every Virasoro minimal model with an $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$ modular invariant. Dividing by a universal product of chiral generalized-minimal-model OPE coefficients reduces the conformal bootstrap problem to a finite algebraic problem governed by root-of-unity quantum-group $6j$ symbols. The exceptional factors of the OPE coefficients can be chosen independent of the second Kac indices $s$, and their dependence on the central charge reduces to finitely many reference cases and explicit phases. A finite computer-assisted calculation yields candidate algebraic $s=1$ seed data and high-precision numerical evidence for existence and uniqueness modulo primary-field signs. We prove that exact existence and uniqueness for these seeds imply the corresponding result for all Kac labels within the genus-zero bulk locality and crossing equations; the finite seed step remains uncertified. The three families require $18$, $32$, and $107$ representative reduced OPE coefficients for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, respectively. We provide reconstruction conventions and coefficient tables for both unitary and nonunitary models. Our calculation assumes only Virasoro symmetry, bulk locality (permutation symmetry) and OPE associativity (crossing equations).
summary: This paper calculates the full set of bulk OPE coefficients for Virasoro minimal models associated with $E_6, E_7,$ and $E_8$ symmetries. By leveraging the conformal bootstrap and reducing the problem to algebraic constraints involving quantum-group symbols, the authors provide explicit, systematic results for these coefficients. This work is crucial for understanding the structure of highly symmetric, exactly solvable quantum field theories.
main_problem: To explicitly calculate the bulk Operator Product Expansion (OPE) coefficients for all Virasoro minimal models possessing an exceptional modular invariant ($E_6, E_7, E_8$).
main_result: The authors provide explicit coefficient tables and reconstruction conventions for these coefficients, reducing the problem to a finite algebraic structure governed by quantum-group 6j symbols.
method: The calculation uses the conformal bootstrap approach, assuming Virasoro symmetry, bulk locality, and OPE associativity, and reducing the problem by dividing by universal chiral coefficients.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Rational Conformal Field Theories (CFTs), specifically the $E$-series Virasoro minimal models, which are characterized by their modular invariance related to the exceptional Lie groups $E_6, E_7, E_8$.
key_observables: Bulk-primary OPE coefficients ($C_{IJK}$), which are required in specific numbers (18 for $E_6$, 32 for $E_7$, 107 for $E_8$).
important_parameters: The central charge $c$ and the Kac indices $(r, s)$ defining the primary operators.
main_assumptions: The calculation assumes only Virasoro symmetry, bulk locality (permutation symmetry), and OPE associativity (crossing equations); the initial seed step remains uncertified.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the paper provides coefficient tables and reconstruction conventions.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the problem, details the reduction to an algebraic problem, presents the results for the three exceptional families, and discusses the implications for existence and uniqueness across all Kac labels.
why_interesting: The rigorous determination of OPE coefficients in highly constrained CFTs provides deep insights into the structure of quantum symmetries, which underpins many modern approaches to strongly correlated systems and quantum field theories.
